newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to renew efforts on Cyprus peace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to renew efforts on Cyprus peace.

text.p: The United States, gravely concerned about Cyprus' plans to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles, will renew this weekend efforts to reduce tensions between Greeks and Turks on the divided island, officials said Tuesday.
They said Carey Cavanaugh, who heads the office of southern European Affairs, would visit Cyprus on Sunday and Monday, seeking to advance a political settlement there.

"He's going in the same context that he's gone in the past, which is to look at ways to bring ideas to the parties on Cyprus in an attempt to lower tensions and bring an end to the conflict that's existed there for decades," State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said.
These ideas include persuading Greeks and Turks to decrease military exercises, like overflights, and promote safety along the U.N.-patrolled ceasefire line in Cyprus.

In an unusually strong statement, the United States Monday deplored Cyprus' contract to buy the S-300 anti-aircraft missile system from Russia, saying it would introduce a destabilising new military element and complicate peace moves.
Cyprus Tuesday rejected the U.S. criticism and Davies said it was not expected that Cyprus would not scuttle the deal.
But U.S. officials said Cavanaugh would again raise Washington's objections to the purchase when he meets Cypriot officials.

Before arriving in Cyprus, Cavanaugh will accompany Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum to The Hague for a meeting of European Union officials and concerns about Cyprus will be be a major topic of their discussions, U.S. officials said.

Kornblum and Cavanaugh plan to leave Washington Thursday for The Hague. Cavanaugh plans to meet officials in Greece early next week and then will visit Turkey at mid-week, officials said. Arrangements were still being made, they said.
Efforts to reunite Cyprus' Greek and Turkish communities, split by a U.N.-patrolled ceasefire line since Turkey's 1974 invasion, under a federal system gathered pace recently.
